steps: The Precision Turning operation, performed on a CNC Turning Center for 17 minutes using a custom CNC program with a spindle speed of 1500 rpm and tool offsets of 0.2 mm, transforms a Shaft Blank into a Machined Shaft.

Using a Grinding Machine, perform Surface Grinding on a Planed Shaft from the Conveyor Belt for 25 minutes with an Aluminum Oxide grinding wheel, a wheel speed of 1800 rpm, and a feed rate of 0.05 mm/pass to produce a Ground Shaft on the Conveyor Belt.

The Horizontal Lathe performs Rough Turning on a Steel Bar for 65 minutes, using a Carbide Insert tool at a rotation speed of 1200 rpm and a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev, transforming it into a Lathed Shaft placed on the ConveyorBelt.

The Broaching Machine performs Keyway Broaching on a MetalBar Shaft Blank for 31 minutes using a Carbide Tipped broach, a feed rate of 0.1 mm/pass, and a depth of cut of 5 mm to produce a Broached Shaft, which is then placed on a ConveyorBelt.

Using a Gear Shaper for Gear Shaping, a Broached Shaft from the ConveyorBelt is transformed into a Shaped Gear on the ConveyorBelt, with parameters set to produce a Spur Gear with 20 teeth at a shaping speed of 100 strokes/min, for 80 minutes.

The Honing Machine performs Bore Honing on a Cylinder for 64 minutes using a 320 grit size, completing 2 passes to achieve a bore size of 50 mm, transforming the Cylinder into a Honed Cylinder, which is then placed on the Conveyor Belt.

Using a Bandsaw for 30 minutes, the operation cuts a Steel Bar (MetalBar) from a MobileRobot into a Cut Bar (LathedPart) placed on a ConveyorBelt with a saw speed of 50 m/min, a Bi-Metal blade, and a cutting width of 3 mm.

The Stewart Platform Mills performs 5-Axis Milling on a Milled Shaft for 36 minutes using a Ball Nose End Mill with a milling precision of 0.01 mm and active vibration damping, transforming it into a Ground Shaft placed on the conveyor belt.

The Vertical Milling Machine performs Contour Milling on a Lathed Shaft for 99 minutes using an End Mill at 800 rpm with a depth of cut of 2 mm, transforming it into a Milled Shaft placed on the conveyor belt.

The Horizontal Milling Machine performs Face Milling on a Milled Shaft from the ConveyorBelt for 16 minutes using a milling speed of 1000 rpm, a spiral tool path, and achieving a surface finish of 0.8 Ra, resulting in a Finished Shaft placed back on the ConveyorBelt.

The Gear Hobbing operation transforms a Broached Shaft into a Hobbied Gear using a Hobbing Machine for 32 minutes, with a hobbing speed of 150 rpm, a feed rate of 1 mm/rev, and an involute gear profile.

Using a Drill Press for 3 minutes, perform Through Hole Drilling on a Steel Bar retrieved from a MobileRobot, creating a Drilled Bar placed on a ConveyorBelt, with a 10 mm drill size, 600 rpm spindle speed, and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev.

Using a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine), the Precision Cutting operation precisely cuts a Shaped Shaft from the ConveyorBelt into a Finished Shaft in 28 minutes with electrical parameters set to 50 V and 10 A, a brass wire, and a cutting speed of 2 mm/min.

The Shaper machine performs Flat Shaping on a Milled Shaft for 79 minutes using a High-Speed Steel tool with a stroke length of 200 mm and a shaping speed of 20 strokes/min, transforming it into a Shaped Shaft.

The Planer performs Surface Planing on a Milled Shaft for 1 minutes with a planing depth of 0.5 mm, a feed rate of 10 m/min, and a surface finish of 1.6 Ra, transforming it into a Planed Shaft on the Conveyor Belt.

The Vertical Lathe performs a turning operation on a Steel Bar for 50 minutes, using a rotation speed of 1000 rpm, a carbide insert tool, and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, transforming it into a Lathed Bar.

The Laser Cutter performs laser cutting on an Aluminum Sheet for 94 minutes at a laser power of 2000 W, a cutting speed of 1 m/min, and with nitrogen gas assist, transforming the sheet into a Cut Sheet that is then placed on a Conveyor Belt.

The Shear (Sheet Metal) machine performs a shearing operation on an Aluminum Sheet from a MobileRobot for 31 minutes at a shear angle of 1 degree, a cutting speed of 0.5 m/min, and using a straight blade, resulting in a Sheared Sheet placed on a ConveyorBelt.

The Punch Press performs the Punching operation on an Aluminum Sheet for 87 minutes, using a 20 mm punch size, a stroke speed of 30 strokes/min, and a die alignment of 0.1 mm, transforming it into a Punched Sheet.

Using Screw Machines, the Threading operation processes Lathed Shafts from the ConveyorBelt into Screwed Shafts for 94 minutes, with an M10 screw size, Metric thread type, and a production rate of 10 parts per minute.

The Shaper machine performs a Shaping operation on a Gear Shaft for 71 minutes, using a Carbide tool with a stroke length of 200 mm and a shaping speed of 30 strokes/min, transforming the MilledPart into a ShapedPart.

Using a Hobbing Machine, a broached Gear Shaft from a conveyor belt is transformed into a hobbied gear by hobbing at a speed of 100 rpm and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev with an involute gear profile, completing the operation in 86 minutes, after which the finished gear is placed back on the conveyor belt.

The Wire EDM operation uses a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) to precisely cut the Gear Shaft into a PrecisionFinishedPart with electrical parameters of 120 V and 20 A, a brass wire, and a cutting speed of 2 mm/min, taking 16 minutes to complete.

The operation involves sawing a metal bar Gear Shaft into a lathed part using a bandsaw for 79 minutes, with a saw speed of 50 m/min, a bi-metal blade, and a cutting width of 2 mm, where the input and output components are both placed on a conveyor belt.

The Gear Shaping operation transforms a BroachedComponent Gear Shaft into a ShapedGear using a Gear Shaper for 92 minutes, shaping a 20-tooth Spur gear at a speed of 40 strokes per minute, with both input and output components remaining on the ConveyorBelt.

Using a Horizontal Lathe, a Gear Shaft made of metal is turned into a lathed part for 79 minutes at a rotation speed of 500 rpm with a carbide insert tool and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, transferring it from the conveyor belt as input and returning it to the conveyor belt as output.

The Grinding operation uses a Grinding Machine for 63 minutes to grind the Gear Shaft planed part into a ground part using an aluminum oxide grinding wheel at a wheel speed of 1800 m/min and a feed rate of 0.05 mm/pass, with both input and output components handled on a conveyor belt.

The CNC Turning Center performs CNC Turning for 10 minutes using a custom G-code program, a spindle speed of 800 rpm, and tool offsets of 0.1 mm to transform a lathed Gear Shaft from the conveyor belt into a finished machined component returned to the conveyor belt.

Using a Vertical Lathe, the MetalBar Gear Shaft is subjected to Vertical Turning for 47 minutes at a rotation speed of 400 rpm, a feed rate of 0.15 mm/rev, and with a ceramic insert tool, transforming it into a LathedPart Gear Shaft on the conveyor belt.

The Planer performs the Planing operation on the Gear Shaft, a MilledPart sourced from the ConveyorBelt, for 64 minutes with a planing depth of 0.5 mm, a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev, and a surface finish of Ra 1.6, resulting in a PlanedPart placed back onto the ConveyorBelt.

The Vertical Milling Machine performs milling on a lathed Gear Shaft for 56 minutes using an end mill at 1200 rpm with a 2 mm depth of cut, transforming it into a milled Gear Shaft, which is then placed on the conveyor belt.

The Honing Machine performs a honing operation on a Gear Shaft (a HonedCylinder) for 4 minutes using a 320 grit size, a 30 s cycle time, and a 50 mm bore size, transforming it into a PrecisionFinishedPart on the ConveyorBelt.

The Gear Shaft, initially a MetalBar on the ConveyorBelt, is drilled into a DrilledComponent using a Drill Press for 87 minutes, with a 10 mm drill, a spindle speed of 600 rpm, and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev.

The Broaching Machine performs an Internal Broaching operation on a MetalBar Gear Shaft for 16 minutes, using a feed rate of 0.05 mm/stroke and a depth of cut of 0.5 mm, transforming it into a BroachedComponent and placing it back on the ConveyorBelt.

The Punch Press performs a punching operation on a Gear Shaft made of sheet metal for 43 minutes, using a 15 mm punch, a stroke speed of 20 strokes per minute, and a die alignment with a 0.1 mm tolerance, transforming the component into a finished sheet metal product on the conveyor belt.

The Laser Cutting operation cuts a SheetMetal Gear Shaft into a CutSheetMetal Gear Shaft using a Laser Cutter for 70 minutes, with a laser power of 2 kW, a cutting speed of 1 m/min, and nitrogen gas assist, transforming the component while keeping it on the ConveyorBelt.

The Gear Shaft, initially on the conveyor belt as a milled part, undergoes Horizontal Milling on a Horizontal Milling Machine for 15 minutes at a milling speed of 800 rpm using a contour tool path to achieve a surface finish of Ra 0.8, resulting in a finished machined component placed back on the conveyor belt.

Using Screw Machines, the Gear Shaft, initially a LathedPart on the ConveyorBelt, undergoes Threading for 27 minutes to produce the ScrewedComponent, employing an M8 screw size with Metric thread type at a production rate of 50 parts/hour.

Perform Precision Milling on the Gear Shaft, a MilledPart, using the Stewart Platform Mills for 99 minutes with a milling precision of 0.01 mm, 6-axis tool configuration, and active vibration damping, transforming it into a GroundPart on the ConveyorBelt.

The Shear (Sheet Metal) machine performs shearing on a Gear Shaft made of SheetMetal for 37 minutes, using a carbon steel blade at a cutting speed of 10 m/min and a shear angle of 1 degree, transforming it into ShearedSheetMetal while keeping it on the ConveyorBelt.

Using a CNC Turning Center for 81 minutes, the Turning operation transforms a Lathed part on a ConveyorBelt into a Finished machined component by executing CNC Program XYZ with a spindle speed of 1200 rpm and tool offsets of 0.1mm.

The Broaching Machine performs broaching with a slab broach at high precision for 32 minutes, transforming a lathed part from the conveyor belt into a broached component placed back onto the conveyor belt.

Using a Punch Press for 76 minutes, sheet metal from the conveyor belt is precisely punched with a 10mm punch at a stroke speed of 30 strokes/min, resulting in a finished sheet metal product placed back on the conveyor belt.

The milling operation uses a Horizontal Milling Machine for 80 minutes at a speed of 2000 rpm with a contour tool path to create a smooth surface finish, transforming a milled part from the conveyor belt into a finished machined component placed back on the conveyor belt.

The Gear Shaping operation shapes a broached component into a 24-tooth spur gear using a Gear Shaper for 19 minutes at a speed of 60 cuts per minute, resulting in a shaped gear ready for further processing.
Using a Drill Press for 6 minutes, the broached component is drilled to create a finished part with holes, achieving a hole diameter of 5mm with a tolerance of ±0.05mm.

Using a Vertical Lathe, perform Turning on a drilled component from the conveyor belt for 37 minutes with a complex toolpath and high precision level to produce the final drilled and shaped part, which is then placed back on the conveyor belt.
The Laser Cutter performs Laser Cutting on sheet metal for 59 minutes at 2000W laser power and 3m/min cutting speed with Nitrogen gas assist, transforming it into cut sheet metal.

The Planer machine performs Planing on a Milled part from the ConveyorBelt for 8 minutes, removing 2mm of material at a feed rate of 10m/min to produce a Planed part with a smooth surface finish, which is then placed back on the ConveyorBelt.

The Screwing operation, performed on Screw Machines for 3 minutes, uses M5 screws with a metric thread type to transform a lathed part from the conveyor belt into a screwed component at a production rate of 120 per hour.
The Shaper machine shapes a milled part into a shaped part by employing a carbide tool with a stroke length of 12mm at a speed of 30 strokes per minute, for 41 minutes.

The milled part from the conveyor belt is subjected to ultra-high precision milling on the Stewart Platform Mills for 79 minutes using a multi-axis tool configuration with active vibration damping, resulting in a ground part placed back on the conveyor belt.
Using a Bandsaw, the metal bar is sawed into a lathed part for 8 minutes at a saw speed of 50m/min with a bimetal blade and a cutting width of 2mm.
The Hobbing Machine performs hobbing on a broached component to create a hobbied gear for 83 minutes, using a hobbing speed of 100 rpm, a feed rate of 0.1mm/rev, and producing a helical gear profile.
Using a Grinding Machine with a diamond grinding wheel at 3000 rpm and a feed rate of 0.05mm per pass, the planed part is ground into a ground part over a duration of 68 minutes.

The Honing Machine performs honing on a honed cylinder for 53 minutes using a 320 grit honing tool, achieving a bore size of 50mm with a cycle time of 5 minutes, transforming the honed cylinder into a precision finished part delivered on the conveyor belt.
The sheet metal is sheared into sheared sheet metal using a Shear (Sheet Metal) machine for 29 minutes with a shear angle of 90°, a cutting speed of 10m/min, and a high-speed steel blade.
Using a Horizontal Lathe for 61 minutes, the Turning operation transforms a Metal bar into a Lathed part with a rotation speed of 800 rpm, a Carbide tool, and a feed rate of 0.2mm/rev.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs Electrical Discharge Machining on a shaped part for 24 minutes using high voltage and a brass wire with a cutting speed of 10mm/min to produce a precision finished part.
The Vertical Milling Machine performs milling operation on a Lathed part for 53 minutes at a speed of 1500 rpm using an End Mill with a depth of cut of 5mm, resulting in a Milled part.

The Screwing operation, performed on Screw Machines for 78 minutes, transforms Lathed parts into Screwed components using an M6 screw size with a Metric thread type at a production rate of 100 units/hour, with both input and output components handled on a ConveyorBelt.

Using a Planer, plane the milled part from the conveyor belt for 99 minutes with a planing depth of 5 mm, a feed rate of 20 mm/min, and a surface finish of Ra 1.6, resulting in a planed part placed back on the conveyor belt.

The Horizontal Lathe performs Lathe Turning on a Metal bar from the ConveyorBelt for 97 minutes using a Carbide Insert tool at a rotation speed of 1200 rpm and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev to produce a Lathed part on the ConveyorBelt.
Using a Broaching Machine for 20 minutes, perform an internal broaching operation on a metal bar with a feed rate of 10 mm/min and a depth of cut of 2 mm to produce a broached component.
Using a Bandsaw for 3 minutes, cut the Metal bar from the ConveyorBelt into a Lathed part on the ConveyorBelt with a saw speed of 50 m/min, a Bi-Metal blade type, and a cutting width of 3 mm.

The Shaper machine performs the Shaping operation, using a High-Speed Steel tool at a stroke length of 100 mm and a speed of 30 strokes/min, to transform a Milled part from the ConveyorBelt into a Shaped part placed back on the ConveyorBelt, for a duration of 1 minute.
The Gear Shaping operation transforms a broached component into a shaped gear with 20 teeth of the spur type on a Gear Shaper machine for 97 minutes, operating at a shaping speed of 15 rpm.

The Horizontal Milling Machine performs milling on a milled part from the conveyor belt for 92 minutes at a milling speed of 800 rpm with a parallel tool path to achieve a surface finish of Ra 0.8, producing a finished machined component placed back on the conveyor belt.

The Hobbing Machine performs hobbing for 43 minutes at a hobbing speed of 100 rpm and a feed rate of 1 mm/rev to create an involute-profile hobbied gear from a broached component, with both the input and output components transported via a conveyor belt.

The Vertical Milling operation transforms a lathed part into a milled part using a Vertical Milling Machine for 11 minutes at a milling speed of 600 rpm with an end mill tool and a depth of cut of 3 mm, with the input part taken from and the output part placed onto the conveyor belt.

Using a Drill Press, a metal bar from the conveyor belt is drilled into a drilled component for 25 minutes with an 8 mm drill, a spindle speed of 1200 rpm, and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev, placing the output back on the conveyor belt.

The CNC Turning Center performs CNC Turning on a lathed part taken from the conveyor belt, using a G-code program, automatic tool offsets, and a spindle speed of 1500 rpm, transforming it into a finished machined component placed back on the conveyor belt, for 31 minutes.

The Shearing operation is performed on the Shear (Sheet Metal) machine for 98 minutes, cutting sheet metal from the conveyor belt into sheared sheet metal using a straight blade at a cutting speed of 30 m/min and a shear angle of 90 degrees.

The Grinding operation uses a Grinding Machine for 73 minutes to grind a Planed part into a Ground part, employing an Aluminum Oxide grinding wheel at 2000 rpm with a feed rate of 0.05 mm/pass, with both parts handled on a ConveyorBelt.

The Laser Cutter performs Laser Cutting on sheet metal for 38 minutes using a laser power of 2 kW, a cutting speed of 10 mm/s, and nitrogen gas assist, transforming the sheet metal into cut sheet metal, which is then placed on the conveyor belt.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs the Wire EDM operation, using a Brass wire and 50 V electrical parameters at a cutting speed of 5 mm/min to transform a Shaped part into a Precision finished part, all processed on a ConveyorBelt for 71 minutes.

Using a Stewart Platform Mills machine for 69 minutes, perform Milling to transform a Milled part into a Ground part with a precision of 0.01 mm, utilizing a Multi-axis tool configuration and Active vibration damping.

The Vertical Lathe Turning operation shapes a metal bar from the conveyor belt into a lathed part on the conveyor belt using a carbide insert tool, with a rotation speed of 1000 rpm and a feed rate of 0.15 mm/rev, for 71 minutes.

The Honing operation refines the Honed cylinder on a Honing Machine for 73 minutes using a 400 grit size, a 5-minute cycle time, and a 50 mm bore size to produce a Precision finished part, with both the input and output components transported via a Conveyor Belt.

The Punch Press performs punching on sheet metal from the conveyor belt for 2 minutes using a 10 mm punch, a stroke speed of 60 strokes/min, and auto die alignment, producing the finished sheet metal product onto the conveyor belt.

The Bandsaw performs the Sawing operation on a Metal Bar for 91 minutes, using a Bimetal blade at 1200 rpm with a cutting width of 5 mm, transforming the Metal Bar into a Lathed Part which is then placed on a MobileRobot.

The Broaching Machine performs the Broaching operation on a Lathed Part for 90 minutes using a Keyway broach with High precision, transforming it into a Broached Component that is then placed on a Conveyor Belt.

Using a Horizontal Lathe, the Turning operation shapes a Metal Bar from a Conveyor Belt into a Lathed Part, which is then placed on a Mobile Robot, for 97 minutes at a rotation speed of 800 rpm, a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, and with a Carbide tool.
The Grinding operation uses Grinding Machines to process a Planed Part into a Ground Part for 24 minutes, utilizing an Aluminum Oxide grinding wheel at 3000 rpm with a feed rate of 0.1 mm/pass.

A Vertical Lathe performs Vertical Turning for 8 minutes at a rotation speed of 1000 rpm with a High-Speed Steel tool and a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev, transforming a Metal Bar from the ConveyorBelt into a Lathed Part placed on a MobileRobot.

The Shaper machine performs the Shaping operation on a Milled Part from the ConveyorBelt for 72 minutes, using a Single Point tool with a stroke length of 10 mm and a shaping speed of 25 cycles/min, resulting in a Shaped Part placed on a MobileRobot.

The Gear Shaping operation uses a Gear Shaper to transform a Broached Component from the ConveyorBelt into a Shaped Gear, which is then placed on a MobileRobot, processing a Spur gear with 20 teeth at a shaping speed of 30 cycles/min for 54 minutes.

The Laser Cutter performs Laser Cutting on Sheet Metal for 67 minutes at a laser power of 2 kW, a cutting speed of 10 mm/s, and using Nitrogen as the gas assist, transforming it into Cut Sheet Metal, which is then moved to the MobileRobot.

The Honing Machine performs honing for 63 minutes using a 320 grit size, a cycle time of 2 minutes, and a bore size of 50 mm to transform a Honed Cylinder from the Conveyor Belt into a Precision Finished Part that is placed on the Mobile Robot.

Using a Shear (Sheet Metal) machine, the Shearing operation cuts a Sheet Metal component from a ConveyorBelt into Sheared Sheet Metal at a shear angle of 1 degree and a cutting speed of 5 m/min with a Straight blade, placing the output onto a MobileRobot, for 39 minutes.

The Punch Press performs punching operation for 76 minutes using a 10 mm punch at a stroke speed of 30 strokes/min with precision die alignment, transforming sheet metal from the conveyor belt into the finished sheet metal product, which is then placed on the mobile robot.

The Planer performs Planing on a Milled Part taken from the ConveyorBelt for 12 minutes, using a Planing depth of 0.5 mm, a Feed rate of 0.3 m/min, and achieving a Surface finish of Ra 0.8, resulting in a Planed Part placed on the MobileRobot.

The Horizontal Milling Machine performs milling at 800 rpm with a linear tool path to achieve a surface finish of Ra 0.4, transforming the Milled Part from the ConveyorBelt into the Finished Machined Component placed on the MobileRobot, for 1 minute.

Using a Drill Press, drill a 6 mm hole in a Metal Bar from the ConveyorBelt for 7 minutes at a spindle speed of 1200 rpm and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev, producing a Drilled Component placed onto a MobileRobot.

The Wire EDM operation uses a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) with parameters set to 50 V, 10 A, a brass wire, and a cutting speed of 5 mm/min to transform a shaped part from the conveyor belt into a precision finished part placed on a mobile robot, taking 46 minutes to complete.

Screw Machining transforms Lathed Parts from the Conveyor Belt into Screwed Components using Screw Machines for 14 minutes, with M8 screw size, metric thread type, and a production rate of 100 pieces per minute, depositing the finished components onto a Mobile Robot.
The Hobbing Machine performs hobbing on a Broached Component for 54 minutes at a speed of 40 rpm and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev to produce an Involute-profile Hobbied Gear.

Using a Vertical Milling Machine, perform Milling on a Lathed Part taken from the ConveyorBelt for 66 minutes at a speed of 1000 rpm with an End Mill tool and a depth of cut of 2 mm, resulting in a Milled Part placed on the MobileRobot.

The CNC Turning Center performs CNC Turning on a Lathed Part taken from the ConveyorBelt, using a CNC program G01, tool offsets of 0.1 mm, and a spindle speed of 1500 rpm, to produce a Finished Machined Component placed on the MobileRobot, for 55 minutes.

The Milling operation transforms the Milled Part into a Ground Part using a Stewart Platform Mills with 6-Axis tool configuration, active vibration damping, and a milling precision of ±0.01 mm, processing the component for 42 minutes and transferring the output to a MobileRobot.

Using a Shear (Sheet Metal) machine, the operation of shearing is performed on sheet metal from a conveyor belt at a shear angle of 45 degrees and a cutting speed of 20 m/min with a straight blade for 67 minutes, resulting in sheared sheet metal that is moved to a mobile robot.

Using a Drill Press, a 5 mm drill is used to perform drilling on a metal bar taken from the conveyor belt for 13 minutes at a spindle speed of 1200 rpm and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev, resulting in a drilled component placed on a mobile robot.

The Punch Press performs a Punching operation on Sheet metal from the ConveyorBelt for 74 minutes using a 10 mm punch, a stroke speed of 30 strokes/min, and aligned dies to produce the Finished sheet metal product, which is then placed on the MobileRobot.

Using a Vertical Lathe, the metal bar is vertically turned into a lathed part for 38 minutes at a rotation speed of 800 rpm, a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, and with a carbide insert tool, with the input material taken from the conveyor belt and the output placed on a mobile robot.

The CNC Turning Center performs CNC Turning for 10 minutes using the 'Bolt finishing' program, a spindle speed of 1500 rpm, and tool offsets of 0.05 mm to transform a Lathed part transported by a MobileRobot into a Finished machined component placed on a ConveyorBelt.

Using a Grinding Machine for 67 minutes, the planed part transported by a MobileRobot undergoes grinding with an aluminum oxide grinding wheel at 1800 rpm and a feed rate of 0.05 mm/pass, resulting in a ground part placed on a ConveyorBelt.

The broaching operation uses a broaching machine to transform a metal bar into a broached component with a push broach, a feed rate of 0.15 mm/rev, and a depth of cut of 2 mm, taking 6 minutes to complete.

Using a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) for 50 minutes, a shaped part is precision-cut into a finished part by applying electrical parameters of 200 V and 12 A, using a brass wire at a cutting speed of 10 mm/min, with the input part delivered by a MobileRobot and the output part transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

The Horizontal Lathe performs Horizontal Turning on a Metal bar for 72 minutes at a rotation speed of 700 rpm, using a high-speed steel tool with a feed rate of 0.25 mm/rev, transforming it into a Lathed part that is then placed on a MobileRobot.

The Horizontal Milling Machine performs horizontal milling on a milled part, carried by a MobileRobot, for 93 minutes at 800 rpm with a contour tool path to achieve a surface finish of Ra 0.8, producing the finished machined component placed on a ConveyorBelt.
The hobbing machine performs hobbing at a speed of 100 rpm and a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev to transform a broached component into a hobbied gear with an involute profile for 25 minutes.

Using a Gear Shaper, the operation of Gear Shaping processes a broached component for 72 minutes to create a shaped gear with a spur gear type, 20 teeth, and a shaping speed of 50 rpm, transferring the input from a MobileRobot and the output to a ConveyorBelt.

The Honing Machine performs honing on a honed cylinder using a 240 grit size, a 30-second cycle time, and a 50 mm bore size for 66 minutes, transforming it into a precision finished part and transferring it to the conveyor belt.

The Bandsaw Cutting operation uses a Bandsaw machine to cut a metal bar from the conveyor belt into a lathed part placed on the mobile robot, lasting 71 minutes with a saw speed of 60 m/min, a bimetal blade, and a cutting width of 3 mm.

The Laser Cutter performs Laser Cutting on sheet metal from the Conveyor Belt, using a laser power of 2 kW, a cutting speed of 1.5 m/min, and nitrogen gas assist, transforming it into cut sheet metal placed on a Mobile Robot, for 18 minutes.

The Vertical Milling Machine performs Vertical Milling on a Lathed part, transforming it into a Milled part, using a tool speed of 1000 rpm, an End mill tool, and a depth of cut of 2 mm, for 77 minutes.

Using a Planer, the operation Planing transforms a Milled part into a Planed part for 27 minutes with a planing depth of 1 mm, a feed rate of 0.5 mm/rev, and a surface finish of Ra 1.6, moving the output to the ConveyorBelt.

On a Shaper machine, a Milled part is shaped into a Shaped part using a single-point tool with a stroke length of 100 mm and a speed of 20 strokes per minute, taking 20 minutes to complete, with the input transported by a MobileRobot and the output placed on a ConveyorBelt.

The Screw Machining operation threads an M6 metric screw into a lathed part using Screw Machines for 97 minutes, producing a screwed component at a rate of 100 parts/hour, with the input part delivered by a MobileRobot and the output transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

Using a Stewart Platform Mills machine with 6-axis tool configuration, 0.01 mm milling precision, and active vibration damping, the Stewart Platform Milling operation processes a milled part from a Mobile Robot into a ground part on a Conveyor Belt in 17 minutes.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs Precision Finishing on a shaped part taken from a conveyor belt, using a brass wire at 15 V with a cutting speed of 2 mm/min, transforming it into a precision finished part placed on a mobile robot, and the operation takes 84 minutes.

Using a Gear Shaper machine for 19 minutes, the operation transforms a broached component into a shaped spur gear with 24 teeth, operating at a shaping speed of 120 rpm, with the input component sourced from a conveyor belt and the output product placed on a mobile robot.

The Laser Cutter performs Laser Cutting on Sheet metal from the ConveyorBelt for 7 minutes using a laser power of 2 kW, a cutting speed of 1.5 m/min, and Nitrogen gas assist, producing Cut sheet metal that is placed on the MobileRobot.

The Shearing operation uses a Shear (Sheet Metal) machine to cut sheet metal at a shear angle of 5 degrees and a cutting speed of 10 m/min with a straight blade for 40 minutes, transforming sheet metal on a conveyor belt into sheared sheet metal placed on a mobile robot.

Using a Punch Press for 73 minutes, the operation involves punching a 10 mm size hole into sheet metal (provided on a conveyor belt) at a stroke speed of 60 SPM with a die alignment of 0.1 mm, resulting in a finished sheet metal product transported by a mobile robot.

The Planer machine performs Planing on a Milled part taken from the ConveyorBelt for 89 minutes with a planing depth of 0.5 mm, a feed rate of 20 cm/min, and a surface finish of Ra 0.8, producing a Planed part that is placed on the MobileRobot.

The Grinding operation uses a Grinding Machine with an Alumina grinding wheel at 1800 rpm and a feed rate of 15 cm/min to process a planed part from the conveyor belt into a ground part, which is then placed on a mobile robot, for 85 minutes.

The Horizontal Milling Machine performs Finish Milling on a milled part from the conveyor belt for 78 minutes at 1000 rpm with a contour tool path and a surface finish of Ra 0.4, producing a finished machined component that is transferred to a mobile robot.

The Honing operation on the Honing Machine processes a honed cylinder from the conveyor belt into a precision finished part, using a honing grit size of 320, a cycle time of 2 minutes, and a bore size of 50 mm, for 29 minutes, with the finished part being placed on a mobile robot.

The Hobbing Machine performs hobbing on a broached component for 89 minutes at a hobbing speed of 500 rpm, a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev, and with an involute gear profile, transforming it into a hobbied gear which is then transferred to a mobile robot.

The Bandsaw performs the Sawing operation for 9 minutes, cutting a Metal bar into a Lathed part using a Bi-Metal blade at a speed of 50 m/min with a cutting width of 3 mm, transferring the output to a MobileRobot.

The Broaching Machine performs a broaching operation using a Push broach, a feed rate of 0.05 mm/stroke, and a depth of cut of 0.2 mm on a metal bar from the conveyor belt, transforming it into a broached component placed on a mobile robot, for 88 minutes.
A Horizontal Lathe performs Turning on a Metal bar for 43 minutes at a rotation speed of 400 rpm, using a Carbide tool with a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev, resulting in a Lathed part.

Using a Vertical Lathe, the metal bar is subjected to vertical turning for 52 minutes at a rotation speed of 300 rpm with a ceramic tool and a feed rate of 0.08 mm/rev, resulting in a lathed part that is then placed on a mobile robot.

The Shaper machine performs the Shaping operation on a Milled part sourced from a Conveyor Belt for 36 minutes using a High-Speed Steel tool with a stroke length of 200 mm and a shaping speed of 30 SPM, producing a Shaped part that is placed on a Mobile Robot.

Using Stewart Platform Mills, the precision milling operation processes a milled part from the conveyor belt into a ground part with a precision of ±0.01 mm using a CBN tool configuration and active vibration damping for 44 minutes, transferring the finished part to a mobile robot.

The CNC Turning operation transforms the lathed part into a finished machined component using a CNC Turning Center for 77 minutes, with a spindle speed of 500 rpm, tool offsets of X 0.02 and Z 0.01, and employing the CNC program G71.
